title: Older Than Shanghai Itself: a 247 AD Temple Ringed by Luxury Malls | China Travel Expert
description:
In the middle of one of Shanghai's glossiest shopping districts sits Jing'an Temple — a Buddhist temple first founded in 247 AD, during the Three Kingdoms period. That makes the temple older than the city of Shanghai itself, which only became a county in 1292.

Here's the honest part: the gleaming gold halls you see today aren't ancient. The temple was damaged last century and the main halls were rebuilt in recent decades, with the current Mahavira Hall completed around 2010 in a Song-dynasty style. So what you're looking at is ancient faith in very modern gold — and it's literally ringed by luxury malls and skyscrapers.

🧭 Expert Tip: go right at opening (around 7:30 am) — the courtyards are calm and photogenic before the shopping crowds roll in.

静安寺始建于公元247年，比上海建城还早；如今金顶大殿是近几十年重建的，四周全是高楼和奢侈品商场——古老的信仰，崭新的金色。
